chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about a man who inherited wealth while the man was absent; is Zakat upon him? He said: No, until he arrives. I said: Does he purify it when he arrives? He said: No, until a year has passed over it and it is in his possession.

key_terms.يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ: A year has passed over it

ai.seo_question: When does Zakat become due on inherited wealth if the heir was absent?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the timing of Zakat obligation for inherited wealth, establishing that the lunar year (Hawl) begins only when the heir actually takes possession, not merely upon the death of the deceased. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that absence or lack of control exempts the heir from immediate liability, ensuring the year completes while the wealth remains in his active possession. This ruling prevents premature financial burden and aligns with the general condition of 'possession' (Habs) required for Zakat to become due.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin marrar, from Yunus, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said,

‘I asked himasws about a man who inherited some wealth, and the man was absent, ‘Would there be Zakāt upon him?’ Heasws said: ‘No, until he comes back’. I said, ‘Would he purify when he comes back?’ Heasws said: ‘No, until a year has passed over it and it is in his possession’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Isma‘ii ibn Marrar from Yunus from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is absent but has inherited a certain asset. Is there Zakat on him? He (the Imam) said, ‘No, Zakat is not due on him until he comes.’ I then asked, ‘Is he required to pay Zakat as soon as he comes?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, until one year passes.’”
